card.name: Buta Kola
card.tagline: Tulu spirit-worship ritual of trance and possession
card.profile: Buta Kola (also Bhuta Kola, Daiva Nema) is a ritual spirit-worship and performance tradition of Tulu Nadu - Dakshina Kannada and Udupi in Karnataka and Kasaragod in Kerala (Wikipedia). A ritual specialist from communities such as the Nalike, Pambada or Parawa is possessed by a bhuta/daiva - spirit of a deified ancestor, hero or natural force - entering a trance to embody the deity in elaborate costume and body-painting, accompanied by music, recital of the spirit's origin-myth in Old Tulu, and dance. The kola honours a single spirit while the nema invokes several; both serve community functions of justice, protection and blessing (Wikipedia; The South First).
card.insight: Closely related to Kerala's Theyyam (regarded as its evolved form), Buta Kola gained wide attention after the 2022 film 'Kantara' depicted its elements, while the ritual remains a living marker of Tuluva identity (HandWiki; Mythlok).
